steps.text: Mix peanut butter, butter or margarine, and sugars until creamy. Stir in vanilla. Beat in eggs. Mix in flour. Stir in 3/4c chocolate chips. Spread dough into a greased 9 x 13 inch pan.
Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 20 to 25 minutes. Remove pan from oven, and sprinkle with the rest of the chocolate chips. Let stand 5 minutes and spread. Cool, and cut into bars.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Butter Bars IV
raw_recipe.description: This recipe forms a rather stiff dough, you might have to press it in the pan. One time I put raisins in the batter by mistake, and my husband loved them that way. You can also omit the chocolate chips and have them plain if you wish.
raw_recipe.name: Peanut Butter Bars IV

review.reviewBody:
I give these a 4 for just the recipe, but I'd give them a 5 with my modifications. The bar part was really good, very peanut-buttery. I left out the chocolate chips in the dough, but I did sprinkle some on top to melt and spread once I took it out of the oven. After it cooled, I made a frosting of peanut butter, powdered sugar, a little milk and a little butter. I spread that on top, then drizzled with more melted chocolate chips. The result was heaven! 
This recipe made a great base, but with the frosting and melted chocolate it was awesome.
Used spelt flour, 1/2c. brown sugar truvia, 1/4c. truvia, and sugar-free Hershey's chocolate chips. Baked at 325 degrees for 25-30 minutes. Perfect!

I always make a double batch and bake in a 12 x 20 pan and leave out 2 eggs (6 eggs for the dbl batch) and add 2 tbl spoons of water to make up for the moisture lost from eggs. I also add a 1/4 cup more peanut butter and have used chunky or walnuts You can use eggs suggested but when you pull pan from oven, hold it 6 or 8 inches above counter top and drop it so the bars drop and are not fluffy. I'would repeat this once or twice , then cool and cut into bars. I aldo use mini chocolate chips but leave out the ones that are to be melted on top.
Incredibly easy. Very tasty. Did the two eggs and 8 tablespoons of butter recommendation and they came out perfect. Using these as Christmas presents.

YUM! I did change it up a bit, so that's why I had to give it 4 stars instead of 5...I used a whole stick (8tbsps.) butter, and only 2 eggs. Also, I baked this in an 11x7 baking pan, and that was the perfect thickness, IMO. I didn't use the chocolate chip topping, but only b/c hubby didn't want it, and they were for him, so... I did use the chips inside the batter, though (mini choco. chip), and that really made these extra tasty. My batter was also not too thick and was easily spread into the pan. Great peanut butter flavor...a keeper! Thanks for sharing. :)

I must start by saying I royally messed up this recipe. I had looked at several others and decided on this, and immediately plopped in a full cup of butter!! So I had to punt, hoping that the simplicity of this recipe would make up for my mistake. Boy did it ever!! I basically doubled the recipe, added a cup or so of uncooked oats, and only half the chocolate chips. We were entertaining a group of women from Spain and Mexico and they thought they were the best cookies ever. One asked for the recipe, and I told her the original, authentic recipe was easy, but I wasn't sure I could reproduce the other, in Spanish. That is my homework. 

If my mistake can't ruin these cookies, nothing can. I say give them a try. I will do them again properly, but for tonight, everyone in my house is very happy with them. Highly recommend.

These turned out great. I was also able to make this gluten free and lowered the sugar. I used a mix of 3 parts millet flour to 1 part each of tapioca flour and sorgum flour. I used a small amount of choc chips in the batter, and skipped the frosting. Thanks for submitting the great recipe!

These are delicious! I followed the recipe exactly, softening the butter and peanut butter in the microwave before adding the sugars and vanilla. These bars have a chewy, moist consistency, much like a brownie. I did leave out the chocolate chips, since we're not big chocolate fans, and I frosted with cream-cheese frosting.

These were pretty good. I made as-is and they werent very peanutty. Next time I will use the whole jar of peanut butter. I also found that after you put on the chocolate chips to pop them back into the oven (turned off) while its still warm-- it helps them melt faster and makes it easier to spread.

I love this recipe, though I agree with what others said about it not fitting in such a big pan. I used a 9"x9" pan and it was just right. I left out the chocolate chips and instead used some boxed chocolates we had gotten for Christmas that had partially melted and re-solidified, so they didn't look nice enough to serve to company anymore. I pressed the chocolates into the dough after it was in the pan so they'd be evenly spaced, and tried to mostly bury them in the peanut butter mixture. The result, I have to admit, was unusual, but our family and guests all enjoyed it. With each bite you never knew what kind of chocolate you were going to find! I named the dish "Buried Treasure", but my husband called it "Land Mine Surprise", and of course that was the name that stuck!
Terrific! Soft and delicious. We did add a little more flour at the end and used 1/2 cup total of mini chocolate chips. Cooked 25 minutes in convection oven. Great recipe.
I make this recipe every year foe co workers and they beg for it!! Looove this recipe!
easy and fast to make for a last minute dessert. Will use this again in a pinch for sure. Yummy

I'm avoiding gluten so instead of flour I put in powdered peanut butter. The resulting bars were squishy in the middle even after baking 10min longer than the recipe said, and I assume it's because of my substitution.

The bars still taste good (bordering on ridiculously sweet...), I just wish they had the "brownie-like" dense chewy texture advertised. I'll try coconut flour next time and see how that goes.

Excellent as written. My only change was to wait longer after sprinkling the chocolate chips over the top of the warm bars. I like having the chips stay intact instead of spreading them, so I let them cool longer before cutting. Thanks for sharing!
Not enough peanut butter taste and not chewy enough.

It tasted da bomb!! I used crunchy peanut butter and it really made a nice texture. The time on the recipe for it to cook is totally WRONG. I checked it after 25 min of baking and it was raw batter. I must've doubled the time. Check the bars with a knife before assuming it is done. Once again, it tasted DA BOMB though.
